# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH ENTEROCOCCI

Enterococcus faecalis is almost always susceptible to penicillins locally,

ampicillin is more effective than vancomycin in susceptible isolates.

Enterococcus faecium is typically resistant to some beta-lactams,

aminoglycosides, and vancomycin. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

# Duration of treatment

For uncomplicated infections where blood cultures are sterile after 24 hours of

treatment, treat for 7-14 days. A longer duration is needed if infection is

complicated or repeat blood cultures are positive.

# Treatment of susceptible E. Faecalis (Van A/B negative)

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-2-gm-iv-q4h)

# Treatment of susceptible E. Faecium (Van A/B negative)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment of resistant enterococcus (Van A/B positive)

[Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h \($$$$\) DI](psjizid-linezolid-600mg-iv-q12h)
